title: WAI spoke restore contract (lives IN basher.json)
description: Validates WAI-Harness/spoke/basher.json including the extended restore block. The restore contract is the restore.items[] list INSIDE the existing spoke basher.json (two-canons guard: no separate restore-contract.json is ever created). Sibling keys of basher.json (spoke, environment, hooks, tooling, propagation, provenance, wiring, schema_version, ...) are allowed and passed through unvalidated beyond basic type shape, so the ~10 existing machine-layer consumers are unaffected. Tier semantics: tracked = delivered by git clone, verified against MANIFEST or git; regenerable = gitignored but derivable, restore RUNS the declared regen_cmd; external = machine-layer need the spoke cannot self-satisfy (secret values, ports, cron, symlinks, provider auth), restore REPORTS it (checklist + needs-lug), never silently skips; ephemeral = gitignored non-derivable history or self-healing runtime byproduct, declared and listed as accepted loss on restore. One artifact MAY span two tiers (canonical case: .env file shell = regenerable from .env.template, secret VALUES = external). Cross-item constraint not expressible in JSON Schema: item ids MUST be unique per contract — enforced by spoke_restore.py --verify.

id.description: Unique per contract (uniqueness enforced by spoke_restore.py --verify).

tier.description: Discriminator; one flat items[] list, tier decides the restore action.

pattern.description: Literal gitignore pattern text this item covers. The --verify gitignore-coverage check matches by EXACT string equality (v1; glob overlap out of scope). Required for tracked, regenerable and ephemeral items; optional for external items (an external need has no on-disk pattern unless it also covers a gitignore line).

verify.description: tracked only: how the clone-delivered tree is verified (manifest = MD5 vs managed MANIFEST.json; git = present in git index).

regen_cmd.description: regenerable only: real shell command run by --restore (cwd = repo root) that materializes the item.

need.description: external only: what the machine layer / operator must supply.

satisfier.description: external only: who/what satisfies the need (basher-machine tool, runbook, operator out-of-band).

note.description: ephemeral: required — why the loss is accepted / how the artifact self-heals. Other tiers: optional clarification.
